name: hay-rack

purpose.role_in_scene: animals eat from it; fill level changes
purpose.why: Rebuilt on Evan's request (2026-10-22) to replace the Ranch tile's original model with a crafted one, keeping its game role.
purpose.audience: children building and playing in a miniature ranch
purpose.style: normal (upgrade: the same asset, built better)

brief.prompt: a wooden slatted hay feeder rack on four legs, V-shaped slats, filled with golden hay

concept.tool: Midjourney web app (midjourney.com/imagine), driven in Evan's signed-in Chrome by Claude through the Claude in Chrome extension, one job at a time, text prompts only (no image reference)

hero.prompt: a wooden slatted hay feeder rack on four legs, V-shaped slats, filled with golden hay, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 1:1
hero.pick_reason: clear V-shaped slatted rack on four legs heaped with golden hay. upscale_clicked is approximate (tool connection dropped)

turnaround.prompt: orthographic turnaround sheet, front view, side view, back view, evenly spaced, same scale, a wooden slatted hay feeder rack on four legs, V-shaped slats, filled with golden hay, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 16:9
turnaround.pick_reason: front, narrower end view and back of one rack, large and well separated

construction.by: modeler agent, directed by the art director (Claude)

rounds.change: First build: 0.95 m rack, V from 0.285 m, legs outside the end boards, slats leaning 24 deg, 0.30 m mound with 88 straw clusters. Hero scored at a guessed 35/30 camera (0.578); the calibration grid then preferred 20/20 (0.724) because the rack was too tall.
Rack lowered to the hero's proportions (rails 0.80 m, V bottom 0.24 m, cross-rail 0.195 m), mound 0.24 m with shorter straw; camera recalibrated to 45/18.
Slats widened and leaned 42 deg the hero's way on the front face, thicker legs, a block where the V boards meet (it hid a dark crossing artefact), hay and pine recoloured to the hero's tan.
Legs moved into the end-frame plane with the cross-rail just outside, end frames at +-0.575 so the rack is 1.3 m long, V bottom lowered to 0.22 m; camera 46/18 (calibration best).

Straw clusters out through both end frames, coarser mound grid to pay for 128 top clusters, muted hay colours; partial, empty and carried variants finished. Final 768 px / 48 samples render and sheet front view scored.

what_was_done: The long side (1.36 m over the top rails) faces the front (-Y). The MJ hero sees that long side on the left and the right-hand (+X) end frame, so it is matched from off the front-right corner.

The hero wins. views/hero.png is the MJ hero keyed on B/G < 0.60 (timber and hay are saturated; the cream backdrop and most of the cast shadow are not), with the floor shadow between the near legs cut away, then closed, hole-filled and opened. The turnaround sheet drew a different, box-shaped rack with X-bracing (no V), so it is used only for the end proportions (legs about 40 % of the height, rail on top). Its left cut, a straight-on long side, is scored as views/view_front.png for reference only; the 3/4 middle view and the duplicate long side are dropped.

hero_check.py renders from the hero's own direction, 46 deg off the front towards +X and 18 deg up, orthographic. Calibrated over a yaw/elevation grid; it agrees with a hand measurement of the hero's edges (about 41-46 deg yaw, about 20 deg elevation).

Timber_Pine, chamfered (11 mm) legs, V boards and top rails. Each end frame is a V of two angled boards (0.095 x 0.055 m) from a small block on the low cross-rail up to the top rails, on two straight legs (0.085 m square) at y = +-0.315 that rise to meet the V boards, joined outside by a low cross-rail. A top rail runs along each long edge, a bottom rail sits in the V, and each V face carries wide diagonal slats (0.11 m, leaning 42 deg, clipped to the end frames) with real gaps. Rack: 1.36 x 0.98 x 0.86 m (V boards poke 5 cm above the rails).

Hay_Gold mound: a lumpy 8 x 6 grid heaped 0.24 m over a ragged rim at the rails, a skirt down to the V faces and a V-shaped underside just inside the slats, so gold shows through every slat gap and through the end V. Straw: clusters of 3-5 folded pointy cards (2 tris each) in Hay_Gold and Hay_Light: over the top (spread wide), along the rim pointing outward, out through the slat gaps and out through both end frames. Full stands 1.12 m to the tips.

One build.py with a STATE switch. full = the hero heap (also hay-rack.glb). partial = a low heap with its rim at 0.58 m, sitting in the bottom half of the V. empty = the bare rack with 16 strands in the bottom of the V and 6 caught in the slats. carried = an armful sheaf alone (0.61 x 0.43 x 0.28 m to the straw tips): a flattened lumpy ellipsoid with straw fanning from both ends and lying along the top, resting on the ground at the origin.

Materials Timber_Pine (timber role), Hay_Gold and Hay_Light (fiber role), flat colours, one material per object: frame, slats, hay, straw_gold, straw_light. Triangles: full 1976 (budget 2k), partial 1242, empty 700, carried 436. No animation, export_animations=False.
construction.creative_additions: Straw poking out through the slat gaps and the end V, and a few strands left caught in the slats of the empty rack.

geometry.up: Z (Blender source); Y in GLB and game
geometry.origin: centre of the footprint, on the ground

good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.837 at 768 px from the calibrated hero camera (0.841 at 384 px).
Reads small as a pine V-feeder with a gold heap: the V end frames, leaning slats and spiky rim carry the silhouette.
Hay shows through the slat gaps and the end V, and straw pokes out of both, as in the hero.
off: Height: the brief said about 0.95 m; the hero's proportions put the rails at about 0.8 m for a 1.3 m length, so the rack follows the hero (0.86 m to the V-board tips, 1.12 m with hay).
The sheet view scores 0.625: it drew a box rack with X-bracing, which the art director told us to ignore.
The hero's heap is a dense mass of fine strands; within 2k triangles it is a faceted mound with about 230 straw cards, so up close it reads coarser and spikier.
The hero's heap leans higher toward the back left; this one is a symmetric dome.
No wood grain: flat colours only, per the game rules.

rights: Original work for Abbie's World. Concept art generated on Evan's Midjourney account; geometry generated procedurally, no third-party meshes or textures.
